elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Both clauses retain automatic renewal ("will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months" / "six (6) months"), so the conditional automatic-renewal elements must all be satisfied; the 30-day opt-out and the 60-day Vendor reminder are absent, so this gateway element fails.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Base Agreement renews for "periods of twelve (12) months"; the Attachment renews for "periods of six (6) months" — both within 12 months.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Both rendered clauses require "sixty (60) days written notice of its intent to terminate" — twice the preferred 30-day opt-out window.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered language; the drafter expressly declined to add one ("rather than upgrading to preferred (30-day opt-out, vendor reminder, CPI cap)").

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewals "shall continue for successive periods under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties," so no unilateral Vendor price increase is permitted — any change needs Customer's written agreement.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Both clauses now read "unless either Party gives sixty (60) days written notice of its intent to terminate" — exactly 60 days in the Base Agreement §4.0 and the Attachment §2.0, replacing the prior six-month and twelve-month windows.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: both clauses preserve "under the same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties," which bars any unilateral uplift; a cap is therefore unnecessary.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: both notice windows are reduced to sixty (60) days, and the retained "same terms and conditions, unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Parties" language means renewal permits no unilateral price increase, so the 5 percent cap element is satisfied by non-application of its condition.

Preferred level is not complete: the 30-day Customer opt-out and the 60-day Vendor pre-renewal reminder are both absent from operative language. To reach preferred the drafter would need to change "sixty (60) days written notice" to "thirty (30) days written notice" for Customer and insert an express Vendor obligation to notify Customer at least sixty (60) days before each renewal date.

Minimality holds: the only textual change in each paragraph is the numeric notice period ("six (6) months" → "sixty (60) days"; "twelve (12) months" → "sixty (60) days"). Renewal term lengths, the termination cross-references to Section 5.0, the three-year initial term, and the same-terms pricing sentence are all retained verbatim; no extras (reminders, CPI formulas, survival tails) were added beyond the chosen fallback checklist.

Intent is preserved: the three-year initial term, Section 5.0 termination rights, Product Attachment incorporation, and the mutual character of the notice right are unchanged, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created. Note for the drafter (not a defect): shortening the mutual window also shortens Vendor's exit notice from six/twelve months to sixty days; if long Vendor-side notice was commercially valuable to us, consider an asymmetric edit shortening only Customer's window while leaving Vendor's longer notice intact.

Both edited paragraphs are covered, which is necessary — leaving the Attachment's twelve-month window (against a six-month renewal term, an unexitable structure and walk-away territory) would have left the fallback incomplete.
